clue.text: Bodyguard on vessel, the post nobody wants

indicators.note: in this down clue the armour is set on, that is attached to, the vessel word

parts.note: a junk is a Chinese sailing vessel
mail is chain armour, a guard for the body

explanation.surface: A bodyguard is stationed aboard a ship, in a posting nobody wants.
explanation.walkthrough: 'post' looks like a job, but it is the mail through the letterbox.
explanation.definitionFit: Unsolicited advertising letters are the post that no recipient wants.

parts.note: read as a gun mounting that rotates, a literally revolving advance in armament, not a political upheaval

explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolutionary' suggests a radical breakthrough; here it means able to turn round.
explanation.definitionFit: A rotating armoured housing for guns on a tank or warship is a revolving piece of firepower.

clue.text: Glaring example of a fabulous killer

definitions.text: Glaring example of a fabulous killer

parts.words: Glaring example of a fabulous killer
parts.note: a creature of fable that kills with its stare, so its murders are literally done by glaring

explanation.walkthrough: 'Glaring example' is an idiom for something obvious; here the monster kills by its glare, and 'fabulous' means from fable.
explanation.definitionFit: The legendary serpent of fable was said to kill anyone with a single look.

indicators.note: the strikebreaker word takes the other letters down inside itself

parts.note: a scab, like a rat, is a worker who breaks a strike

explanation.surface: A rodent gulps down a beetle by the riverbank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rat' looks like the animal but means a strikebreaker.
explanation.definitionFit: The sacred dung beetle of ancient Egypt is a kind of insect.

clue.text: Party when out of range in Turkey, Iran and Russia

indicators.note: the word for when is taken out of the mountain range's name

parts.words: range in Turkey, Iran and Russia
parts.note: the Caucasus mountains span the borders of these countries
as can mean when, as in 'as I left'

explanation.surface: A political group meets when it is beyond the mountains of Turkey, Iran and Russia.
explanation.definitionFit: A closed meeting of a political faction or party's members is a party grouping.

parts.note: horseplay read literally as a game played on horses, polo, and a spell as one of its timed periods

explanation.walkthrough: Horseplay usually means rough fooling about; here it is play on horseback.
explanation.definitionFit: Polo is divided into timed periods of play, each a spell in the game played on horseback.

clue.text: Portly pet — one getting too much bread?

definitions.meaning: bread is slang for money, so a highly overpaid person

explanation.definitionFit: A wealthy, overpaid executive is called this, and literally it is a plump feline pet.

clue.text: Quake, losing heart with a high-pitched voice

indicators.note: the shaking word loses its central letter

parts.note: to quake is to tremble

explanation.surface: Someone shakes nervously and sings in a squeaky tone.
explanation.definitionFit: A boy soprano's voice, the highest singing part, is high-pitched.

clue.text: Red Cross patron goes tearing off

indicators.note: off signals the letters going wrong, being rearranged

explanation.surface: A charity's sponsor rushes away in a hurry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Red Cross' looks like the aid charity; it is the red cross on a white flag of England.
explanation.definitionFit: England's patron saint is honoured by the red cross on the English flag.

clue.text: A trap for the careless driver

definitions.text: A trap for the careless driver

parts.words: A trap for the careless driver
parts.note: the driver is a golfer hitting off the tee, and the trap a sand hazard on the course

explanation.walkthrough: 'driver' suggests a motorist; in golf it is the long club or the person using it.
explanation.definitionFit: A sand-filled hollow on a golf course is a hazard catching wayward shots.

clue.text: Workers will make a beeline for them

definitions.text: Workers will make a beeline for them

parts.words: Workers will make a beeline for them
parts.note: worker bees head straight home to the places where hives are kept

explanation.walkthrough: 'Workers' suggests employees heading to work; these are worker bees.
explanation.definitionFit: Places where beekeepers keep hives are where worker bees fly home.

indicators.note: the other birds' name is turned round to give this one

parts.note: auks are other seabirds, the others besides the defined bird

explanation.surface: A bird that other people look to for help.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn to' looks like seeking help; it signals reading the other birds backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: This predatory seabird, which robs gulls of their catch, is a bird.

parts.note: a racketeer read as a tennis player, and the go-between as the thing passing between the two rackets

explanation.walkthrough: A racketeer is usually a gangster; here a player wielding a racket.
explanation.definitionFit: The fuzzy sphere travels back and forth between the players' rackets on court.

clue.text: Demonstrating a toy, testing public opinion

definitions.meaning: literally sending a toy up on a string in the wind
an idiom for floating an idea to see how people react

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means floating a tentative idea, and literally it is sending a toy aloft on the breeze.

clue.text: Lie in bed, suffering, not fit enough to eat

indicators.note: suffering suggests the words are in a bad way, so their letters are disordered

explanation.surface: Someone lies in bed ill, too poorly to eat.
explanation.definitionFit: Food unsuitable for consumption is not fit enough to be eaten.

parts.note: to top something is to surpass it
a notch is a scored mark or cut

explanation.surface: Beating a match score counts as a great achievement.
explanation.definitionFit: First-rate or of the highest quality means excellent.

parts.note: Sal is a familiar short form of Sarah
low means depressed

explanation.surface: Sarah is feeling down and looks a little bitter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jaundiced' suggests cynical; here it means yellowish in colour.
explanation.definitionFit: A sickly yellowish complexion is somewhat like the colour of jaundice.

parts.note: AB is an able seaman, a jack tar, with the 's giving S
U means upper-class, posh
RD is short for road, a way

explanation.surface: Jack's smart manner of behaving looks silly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jack' as a sailor is a crossword convention; U for upper-class comes from 1950s British usage.
explanation.definitionFit: Something preposterous or nonsensical is ridiculous.

parts.note: battled means fought
the ore is a coin of Sweden, Denmark and Norway

explanation.surface: People clashed in a noisy dispute over money from abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'racket' looks like noise or a scam; it is the bat of an old shuttlecock game.
explanation.definitionFit: The wooden bat used in the old game with a shuttlecock is a small racket.

parts.note: a nursery read as a plant nursery, and the scoop a small hand tool for digging, not a news story

explanation.walkthrough: 'nursery' suggests children and 'scoop' a news exclusive; here plants and a hand spade.
explanation.definitionFit: A small hand tool for digging in a garden or plant nursery is a little scoop.

clue.text: Ex-star possibly seen in crowd scenes

definitions.note: a description phrase standing for the people who are so seen

indicators.note: possibly says the letters might be arranged another way

explanation.surface: A former celebrity may now turn up only among the background actors.
explanation.definitionFit: Background performers in films fill the crowd scenes without speaking parts.

clue.text: Boozers turn up with a bottle opener and start to sing

indicators.note: turn means the short word after it is turned round
a bottle opener here is the opening letter of the word bottle
the start of the word sing gives its first letter

explanation.surface: Drinkers appear carrying a corkscrew and begin to sing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boozers' looks like drinkers; in British slang a boozer is also a pub.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang, a boozer is a tavern where alcohol is drunk.

parts.note: all means everyone
owing means in debt, in arrears

explanation.surface: Confessing that everybody is behind with payments.
explanation.definitionFit: Letting someone in or granting permission is admitting them.

definitions.meaning: ... as in began a hobby or idea
... as in shortened a hem, or lifted

explanation.definitionFit: Adopting a hobby and raising something like a hem are both senses of this phrasal verb.

parts.note: W is the abbreviation for west or western
heels are villains or cads

explanation.surface: A cowboy film full of villains and six-guns.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolvers' suggests pistols in the Western; here it means things that go round.
explanation.definitionFit: Things that revolve around an axle are rotating parts of a vehicle.

parts.note: ran means directed or managed
CID is the Criminal Investigation Department of the British police

explanation.walkthrough: 'offensive' looks like an attack noun; it is the adjective meaning foul-smelling.
explanation.definitionFit: Rotten, foul-smelling food is unpleasant and offensive to the senses.
